note: 1.5 release readiness umbrella, created at Fabio's request after an umbrella review of the whole board. Gate list only - it re-parents nothing, exactly as MPI-450 did for 1.4. Measured 2026-08-21: 1.4.2 on disk, 163 commits since the tag, release:check passed, UNRELEASED.md carries 12 bullets with features present, so the cut is 1.5.0.

Retargeted 1.5 -> 2.0 at Fabio's request - he asked whether the card was stale enough to delete. It is not: all seven Gate A cards (507, 515, 527, 522, 523, 516, 575) are still todo and every one has an updated_at OLDER than the card, so nothing on the gate list was fixed. Only the version label and the measured snapshot were stale. Snapshot DELETED rather than refreshed (163 commits -> 356, 12 UNRELEASED bullets -> 25, 5 flows -> 8 in the notes and 9 in the registry, 3 doing -> 5) and replaced by an ON PICKUP re-measure list, so the card stops rotting. New Gate C items: the notes/registry Flow-list disagreement (voice-changer is in flowsRegistry.js and in no bullet), whether a MAJOR digit owes a migration note, and re-adjudicating the four cards excluded under a 1.5 scope. MPI-567 and MPI-594 dropped off the loose-Flow-card list - both done.

Two Gate C questions ANSWERED by Fabio 2026-08-26. (1) WHY MAJOR: Flows make it major, on AUDIENCE not code - no migration or compat note is owed. Flows open the app to a user who could not use it before, or for whom it was hard; they are extremely simple and straightforward and will draw a different kind of user. Plus a competitive half that belongs in the release body: some of these Flows exist NOWHERE ELSE, or only behind proprietary websites. (2) THE FLOW LIST IS STILL GROWING - more Flows land before 2.0 cuts, so no number can be pinned now. The gate was reframed from 'freeze the list' to a mechanical reconcile run ONCE, immediately before the notes freeze: diff flowsRegistry.js ids against the Flows named in UNRELEASED.md and fix the count sentence. The 8-vs-9 voice-changer drift is kept as the worked example, not as the answer. Fabio also confirmed the card stays - keep, do not delete.
